title: Stop the admin console looking its operations up on every request

blocks.text: The admin console lets operators run operations on live service objects by name: `resize` with an `int` on a thread pool, `restart` on a worker, `drain` (a private method) before a deploy. A profile of the console under a load test shows most of its time in `Class.getDeclaredMethod`, called once per request, although the console only knows a few dozen operations.

items: `method(...)`: the method a request needs, ready to invoke;
`key(...)`: what the method is cached under.

blocks.text: When you're done, each operation is looked up on its first request only, every request still runs the method it names, and private operations run. About eight lines in total.
The tests count the lookups through the `Finder` the constructor takes.

cases.says: an operation requested again, on the same object or another of its class, reuses the method found the first time
a private operation runs, and runs again without a second lookup
two operations with the same name and different parameter types each run their own method
operations of two classes with the same simple name in different outer classes each run their own method

origin.section: Looking a Method Up Costs More Than Calling It, So Look Up Once

concepts: Looking a method up costs several times the call and returns a new Method each time, so a cache keyed by class, name and parameter types looks each method up once and stores it already accessible.
